The Degrees of Freedom That a Summary Reports

Source: R/inference.R
summary_edf.Rd

Returns the table of effective degrees of freedom that summary.StatmodFit() reports, read on the information of the variance convention vcov_type, and a note where that information is the observed one and is indefinite at the estimate.

Usage

summary_edf(object, vcov_type, spec, design)

Arguments

object

A StatmodFit().

vcov_type

A vcov_method object.

spec, design

The specification and the design of the fit.

Value

A list with edf (the table, in the shape of fit@edf), info (the information object that the table was read on, or NULL where the fit does not record it) and note (a string, empty where there is nothing to report).

Details

The table stored in the fit, fit@edf, was read on the information of the outer criterion (reml(), ml(), aic() or bic()) or, where there is none, on the inner information; the fit records that information in fit@methods$edf_information. The standard errors of a summary read the information of vcov_type, so the table is recomputed on that matrix when the two differ, and the count printed beside a standard error is a share of the same \(H\).

The table stored in the fit is kept in three cases: a criterion that prices the fit with the count (aic() or bic()) reads the count on its own information, and a summary that recomputed it would no longer reproduce that criterion; a model with a structural term of the likelihood shape (modelterms7::regime(), a marginal break-point term), which has no expected information; and a variance convention without an information property has no matrix to read. A model with a score-driven filter reads the joint vector of the coefficients and the filter's parameters, on the observed information or on the expected information conditional on the past.

The eigenvalues of \((H+S)^{-1}H\) are \(v^\top H v/(v^\top H v + v^\top S v)\) for the eigenvectors \(v\) of the pencil, which lie in \([0, 1]\) for a positive semidefinite \(H\). A direction with \(v^\top H v < 0\) contributes a negative share, so the count of a term can fall below its true value, and the total can leave \([0, p]\). The observed information is tested for this by its Cholesky factor and, where that fails, by the smallest eigenvalue: the matrix is indefinite when that eigenvalue is below \(-p\,\epsilon\,\lambda_{\max}\), the floor with which solve_pd() and pd_logdet_dense() separate a flat direction from rounding.

See also

statmod_edf(), vcov_information()
